question.problem:
The equation $2{x}^{2}+5x-9=0$ has{{field-1}}
distinct real solutions.
question.worked_solution:
To quickly determine the number of solutions, we can compute the discriminant. We have $a=2,$ $b=5,$ and $c=-9,$ so the discriminant is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={b}^{2}-4ac \\  & ={5}^{2}-4(2)(-9) \\  & =25+72 \\  & =97\end{aligned}
$$

Since the discriminant is positive $(D>0),$ the equation has $2$ distinct real solutions.
